content:
sam: incident-bot fired: CANARY_FAILURE_RATE_HIGH for eu-canary-1 — 22% failing in last 5m :rotating_light:
incident-bot: Alert details: metric=canary_failure_rate, env=eu, probe=eu-canary-1, window=5m, threshold=0.05
maya: seeing it too, console shows a big spike around 13:03 UTC. looks correlated with a deploy?
oliver: I don't see a deploy in the window. last deploy was 12:40 and was a small config change for logging.
rachel: customer impact? any 500s from production traffic?
sam: pager logs show only synth probes failing, production traffic error rate steady at baseline. quick check: no customer-facing 5xx alerts.
maya: ok that's good. could be probe sensitivity or a flaky dependency in the canary harness.
incident-bot: Related alerts: synth-probe-tx-latency-high (eu-canary-1) — 1m ago
oliver: proposal: suppress the eu-canary-1 alert group to stop paging while we investigate, keep the metric recorded. I can flip the suppression and adjust threshold.
rachel: +1 to suppress, but let's log mitigation steps and handoff to next oncall.
sam: I'm going to mute the alert for 30m while we triage. will also set a short-term threshold bump from 5% -> 12% so we don't mask a real regression (we'll still record raw metric).
maya: please paste the commands you used so we can reproduce in runbook.
sam: doing it now:
```
# temporary alert mute
curl -X POST "https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/mute" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"alert":"canary_failure_rate:eu-canary-1","duration":"30m","reason":"investigating flapping probes"}'

# bump threshold
curl -X PATCH "https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"alert":"canary_failure_rate","scope":"eu","threshold":0.12}'
```
oliver: copied commands to incident runbook page: https://console.redwood/incident-runbooks/synth-flap-2026 — added a checklist
rachel: can someone check the probe host logs? might be network flaps to the synthetic runner in eu-west-2.
maya: digging in now — tailing /var/log/canary/runner.log on canary-03 shows transient connection timeouts to the backend inference pool at 13:02-13:04.
sam: that matches the spike window. backend host list shows a couple nodes with high CPU around that time. could be noisy neighbor on Dedicated pool.
oliver: good catch. I'll tile an infra page to see if any autoscale or eviction events happened.
incident-bot: infra-alert: node_eviction_detected on pool-dedicated-7 — 13:01 UTC
maya: okay there we go. eviction caused brief request failures that the probe amplified. not an app regression.
rachel: customer impact still low, but need to avoid alert storms. action items: 1) revert temp threshold after 30m 2) tune probe to reduce false positives 3) add dashboard and SLO correlation 4) add an automatic suppression rule when node_eviction_detected fires
sam: logging the items in the post-incident card. also adding notify to oncall rotation for handoff.
oliver: I'll create the dashboard: synth -> probe success rate vs infra evictions, include 1h heatmap and per-probe histograms. linking: https://monitor.redwood/dashboards/synth-eviction-correlation
maya: probe tuning suggestion: increase sampling frequency backoff and require 2 consecutive failures within 3m before firing. here's a suggested rule snippet:
```
# suggested probe config
probe.name: eu-canary-1
probe.frequency: 30s   # reduce noise from 10s to 30s
probe.failure_window: 180s  # 3m window
probe.failure_threshold: 2  # require 2 failures in window
```
rachel: that sounds reasonable. add to repo PR and flag for review by eng-runtime for possible graceful backoff logic.
sam: Handoff: I'm going offline in 10m. @oliver you're on next for the rotation. please monitor the mute expiry and revert the threshold to 5% if infra looks stable. I've set a calendar reminder at 13:40 UTC.
oliver: copy. I'll watch the mute and the infra events. also will kick off a retention job to keep the raw probe traces for 7d for debugging.
maya: ephemeral note — we should consider a global policy: when node_eviction_detected fires, auto-suppress synth alerts for 10m for that region. reduces noise and points operators to infra. I'll add a RFC to eng-sre backlog.
rachel: agreed. capture in ticket: https://jira.redwood/browse/OPS-5824 (added). owners: eng-sre + eng-runtime.
incident-bot: Alert mute expired for canary_failure_rate:eu-canary-1 (30m) — 13:41 UTC
sam: back online, checking status — probe is now at 1.8% failure, infra nodes recovered. I'll revert the threshold patch now.
sam: revert command:
```
curl -X PATCH "https://ops.redwood.internal/alerts/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"alert":"canary_failure_rate","scope":"eu","threshold":0.05}'
```
oliver: threshold reverted. dashboard looks green. closing thread, moving follow-ups to OPS-5824 and postmortem notes in runbook. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
rachel: nice quick triage team. add a note to customer success that this was infra-related and no customer action required.
maya: done. CS notified via #customer-success (message id linked).
sam: wrapping up: summary for postmortem — root cause: node eviction in dedicated inference pool; symptom: synthetic probe amplified transient failures due to sensitive probe config (10s freq, single failure threshold); mitigation: temporary alert mute and threshold bump, infra autoscaling stabilized pool; long-term: probe config changes, dashboard, auto-suppression on eviction.
oliver: filing the short postmortem and linking tickets.
incident-bot: Thread marked resolved by sam at 13:46 UTC
